entries.name: Gambel's quail
behaviour: walks in coveys; sprints into brush rather than flying when startled
breeds boom after rains; one to two broods a year
gets its water from green forage

voxel_model.pattern: comma-shaped black topknot, chestnut flanks

entries.notes: The covey quail of the Sonoran; a common prey animal and a classic desert scene-setter. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Cactus wren
behaviour: builds a football-sized domed nest lined with feathers inside cholla and saguaro
largest wren in the US; state bird of Arizona
males build several nests; pairs raise up to three broods a year

voxel_model.pattern: white eyebrow stripe, heavily spotted and barred brown and white

entries.notes: Arizona's state bird; nests wedged inside cholla are both impregnable and a lovely detail for voxel cacti. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Gila woodpecker
behaviour: excavates nest boots inside living saguaro cactus; old cavities shelter owls, kestrels and flycatchers
rolls a loud churring call while drumming on chimneys and pipes
two to three broods a year

voxel_model.pattern: black-and-white ladderback, red crown patch on males

entries.notes: The architect of the saguaro: every other cavity-nesting Sonoran bird is its tenant. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Chinkara (Indian gazelle)
behaviour: state animal of Rajasthan; hangs around desert villages guarded by the Bishnoi community
territorial bucks hold small plots marked with dung middens
can run 50-60 km/h across loose sand dunes

voxel_model.pattern: reddish-buff summer coat, white belly, S-shaped annulated horns

entries.notes: The Thar desert's sacred gazelle; Bishnoi protection is why it survives near settlements.

entries.name: Desert cottontail
behaviour: nests in shallow fur-lined scrapes; four to six litters a year
reingests soft droppings to get at what the gut missed
freezes motionless under brush to use its camouflage

voxel_model.pattern: rufous nape patch, white cottony tail underside

entries.notes: The most common rabbit of the dry country; breeds prolifically and anchors the coyote-and-owl food web.

entries.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
behaviour: never drinks; lives its whole life on seed moisture alone
cheek pouches haul seeds to sand-dune burrow caches
richocheting zig-zag escape; hind-foot drumming warns neighbours

voxel_model.pattern: dark dorsal stripe, white hip patches

entries.notes: The seed-vault rodent of loose dunes; the ecological engine of the sand-dune desert.

entries.name: Fat sand rat
behaviour: eats only salt-laden halophyte leaves and recycles the salty water; the go-to model for type 2 diabetes
lives in burrow colonies with chambers for sleeping, storing and latrines
dies young when overfed; its wild diet is almost exclusively saltwort

voxel_model.pattern: sandy back, creamy belly and cheeks, tufted tail

entries.notes: A diabetes-research celebrity: a desert rat that lives entirely on salty succulents.

entries.name: Egyptian spiny mouse
behaviour: coat sheds its spines like a lizard drops its tail when grabbed
precocial young born fully furred and open-eyed
family groups help raise the pups; a commensal around desert villages

voxel_model.pattern: ochre-brown spiny back, white belly

entries.notes: The spiny, shed-skinned mouse of wadis and tombs; famous among biologists for near-perfect regeneration.

entries.name: White-throated woodrat (desert packrat)
behaviour: builds towering stick middens up to a cubic metre, glued with amber urine
famously hoards glittering objects — coins, foil, keys — into its nest
gets all its moisture from cactus and browse

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown back, white throat and belly

entries.notes: The original collector: its amber-glued middens preserve 50,000-year-old pollen and packrat mummies.

entries.name: Southern grasshopper mouse
behaviour: howls like a tiny wolf at night to mark its territory
immune to Arizona bark scorpion venom; eats scorpions as a staple
monogamous pairs hunt and nest together

voxel_model.pattern: tan back, white belly, thick pale-tipped tail

entries.notes: A mouse-sized carnivore that sings. Genuinely preys on animals heavier than itself.

entries.name: Rock hyrax (dassie)
behaviour: closest living relative of the elephant; sweats through its feet and has hoof-like nails
suns in colonies on boulders at dawn; designated sentinel keeps watch
males sing loud, falling wails at noon in rocky wadis

voxel_model.pattern: dark dorsal gland patch, yellowish shoulder patch

entries.notes: The stone-loving 'coney' of the Psalms: an ancient, sociable rock-rabbit with elephant ancestry.

entries.name: Pallid bat
behaviour: listens for cricket footsteps and scoops them off the ground — a bat that hunts by ear like an owl
roosts in rock crevices and old buildings in small colonies
hangs in loose groups; audible chirps and rustles from the roost
entries.notes: A ground-hawking bat; the big donkey-ear silhouette over desert rock at dusk.

entries.name: Mexican free-tailed bat
entries.migrates: migrates south in winter; massive columns of mothers with nursing pups
behaviour: Bracken Cave colony: 20 million bats, the largest known mammal aggregation on Earth
mothers find their own pups in a million-bat crowd by voice alone
flies high and fast; moth swarms visibly vanish when a column passes
sounds: roaring emergence howl from cave mouths
entries.notes: The 20-million-strong columns at dusk are one of the great wildlife spectacles of the Americas.

entries.name: Dibatag (Clarke's gazelle)
behaviour: stands on its hind legs like a gerenuk to browse higher thornbush
holds its long black tail upright when alarmed — the name means 'tail-in-the-air'
shy and nearly invisible motionless in thorn scrub

voxel_model.pattern: grey-cinnamon back, white sides and haunches, black tail

entries.notes: Critically rare; surviving only in the Ogaden and central Somalia, never in captivity. A ghost of the Horn of Africa.

entries.name: Namaqua sandgrouse
entries.migrates: nomadic with the rains; flies tens of kilometres daily to distant waterholes
behaviour: males soak their belly feathers at distant waterholes and carry water home to the chicks
drinking flocks number in the hundreds at dawn and dusk
tolerates water far too salty for most birds

voxel_model.pattern: fine barring, male black throat band

entries.notes: The Kalahari's other water-carrier; like its black-bellied cousin, it smuggles water to its young in its plumage. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Verdin
behaviour: tiny grey finch-like bird with a bright yellow head in the male
builds two big twig sphere nests — one breeding, one roosting against the cold desert nights
gleans leaves upside-down like a tiny chickadee
entries.notes: The only New World penduline-tit; a pocket-sized sun spark crashing through the mesquite. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Phainopepla
entries.migrates: short local moves between desert mistletoe stands and riparian elderberry for a second brood
behaviour: silky-flycatcher specialised for desert mistletoe; the seeds must pass through it to germinate
male is jet black with a long crest and scarlet eye
vagrant waxwing-like flocks gather where berries ripen

voxel_model.pattern: red eye, silky black plumage, female grey with streaked crest

entries.notes: The mistletoe bird; wherever velvet mistletoe hangs in the desert, phainopepas will be queuing for it. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Costa's hummingbird
entries.migrates: spends the scorching summer in cooler uplands; arrives early spring for the desert bloom
behaviour: male dives in a U-shape and pops a loud whistle at the bottom of the arc
enters torpor on cold nights to survive dawn cold snaps
one of the smallest warm-blooded vertebrates in the desert

voxel_model.pattern: purple crown and elongated forked gorget on the male

entries.notes: A 3-gram jewel that times its whole life to the February ocotillo bloom. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Isabelline wheatear
entries.migrates: long-distance migrant; winters from the Sahel across Arabia to India
behaviour: nests at the back of gerbil and souslik burrows
cartwheels through the air to snatch a grasshopper mid-flight
pale sandy bird that stands upright and pumps its tail

voxel_model.pattern: sandy body, black throat and eye-stripe, pale rump

entries.notes: The mile-wide wheatear of the great deserts; arrives in Sahara-edge grassland just as the rains end. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Greater hoopoe-lark
behaviour: long decurved bill digs larvae out of loose dunes
one of the few larks nesting in shrubs rather than scrapes
male sings in long undulating song-flight over dunes, swooping down on a whim

voxel_model.pattern: black-and-white wing bars, rufous-and-black wing coverts

entries.notes: The hoopoe-billed lark of old Arabia; its song over empty dunes is near-mythical. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Cream-colored courser
behaviour: runs like a tiny plover rather than flying; freezes flat into the gravel when threatened
stands dead-still in open stony desert, pancaked to the ground
nomadic pairs appear wherever rain brings out termite swarms

voxel_model.pattern: pale cream back, black-and-white head stripes

entries.notes: A sand-coloured ghost of the hammada; invisible until it bolts ten paces under your nose. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common poorwill
behaviour: the only bird known to hibernate; drops its body temperature to near 5°C for weeks on end
sits flat on open sand at dusk calling its name
flies like a giant erratic moth

voxel_model.pattern: cryptic mottled grey-brown, white throat bar

entries.notes: The hibernating nightjar: sits on bare stone all winter with its engine idling at freezing. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Elf owl
entries.migrates: winters in Mexico and Central America
behaviour: world's smallest owl; nests in old gila woodpecker boots inside living saguaros
plucks scorpions and bites off the stinger before eating them
hunts around porch lights like a flycatcher

voxel_model.pattern: fine streaking and dotting, white eyebrows

entries.notes: A four-ounce owl living inside a cactus boot; the tiniest wise head in the desert. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Desert iguana
behaviour: deliberately basks at 46°C, the hottest reptile on Earth
prefers yellow flowers over every other colour
inflates its dewlap and puffs its body as a threat display

voxel_model.pattern: powdery white with grey reticulations and a grey net pattern

entries.notes: The only lizard that sprints around at midday in total sun; a sun-worshipping vegetarian.

entries.name: Zebra-tailed lizard
behaviour: sprints across alkali flats flashing its black-and-white barred tail like a zebra over plains
curls its tail over its back and waves it during courtship or threat
high reproductive turnover; several broods a year under predation pressure

voxel_model.pattern: dotted flanks, black bars and white tail underside

entries.notes: The blur on the playa; its tail signal tells you it saw you first.

entries.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
behaviour: heat-sensing pits find warm rodents in total darkness
often basks by day and hunts by dusk; habit blamed for most human bites
fasts for a year or more between meals

voxel_model.pattern: bold diamond chain along the back, black-and-white banded tail

entries.notes: The characteristic rattler of the desert southwest; respect the rattle and leave it be.

entries.name: Mojave rattlesnake
behaviour: carries Mojave toxin, a neurotoxic venom among the most potent in North America
shy and rarely defensive unless harassed or stepped on
beautiful pink-greenish phase in the far Mojave and Great Basin

voxel_model.pattern: pale green-ochre with dark blotches, black tail bands

entries.notes: Beautiful, secretive and dangerously neurotoxic; the one rattler that can drop a grown human.

entries.name: Desert horned lizard (regal horned lizard)
behaviour: sits motionless over harvester ant trails and licks them up
flat sandy pancake that vanishes completely into gravel
crown of horns and a heart-shaped fringe of spines

voxel_model.pattern: bold pale blotches and dark flank edging, crowned head

entries.notes: The 'horny toad'; entirely dependent on harvester ants, so where ants vanish, it follows.

entries.name: Sand boa
behaviour: swims through loose dunes with a shovel-shaped snout
ambush predator buried snout-deep in sand for days
hunts mainly small mammals and raids lizard nests

voxel_model.pattern: ochre with irregular brown blotches

entries.notes: The Old World answer to the sandfish: a living spade, invisible in the dune.

entries.name: Namaqua chameleon
behaviour: ground-running dune chameleon; darkens to charcoal in the morning to warm up, then pales
drinks fog and dew from its own coiled body and nasal grooves
one of the fastest chameleons alive, hunting over hot open dunes

voxel_model.pattern: bands and blotches; dramatic full-body colour-shifting

entries.notes: The only chameleon that lives entirely on bare dunes; a rule-breaker in a family of tree-dwellers.

entries.name: Peringuey's adder
behaviour: eyes sit right on top of its head to watch while the body is buried
sidewinds across dunes; a third of the population waves a black tail-tip as a lure
ambushes dune lizards from beneath the surface

voxel_model.pattern: orange-buff with faint three-row spotting, often black-tipped tail

entries.notes: The Namib's other sidewinder; the whole world's smallest horned-eye view of a buried world.

entries.name: Webb's web-footed gecko
behaviour: translucent, ghost-pale skin; you can see its heart beating
broad webbed feet act as snow-shoes on loose dunes
drinks fog condensation straight from its own skin

voxel_model.pattern: translucent pale pink with faint marbling

entries.notes: The ghost gecko of the coast dunes; semi-transparent and utterly weightless.

entries.name: Barking gecko
behaviour: males call from burrow mouths at dusk in near-unison, a desert chorus
fringed toes grip sliding sand; lives head-down in self-dug burrows
the call carries over a kilometre on still evenings
sounds: loud barking gecko calls at dusk

voxel_model.pattern: mottled sandy brown with pale spots

entries.notes: At sunset the whole Kalahari barks; a dusk chorus of hundreds of tiny geckos.

entries.name: Speckled padloper
behaviour: world's smallest tortoise; shell plates gleam like a painted pebble
walks slowly between succulent clumps after the winter rains
flirts with nods and head-bobs; aestivates through the dry summer

voxel_model.pattern: speckled shell with bold dark and pale markings

entries.notes: Endangered; the jewel of the Succulent Karoo badlands, halved by pied crows over decades.

entries.name: Desert rain frog
behaviour: spends months underground; surfaces only after fog or rain
squeaks like an angry dog when handled or alarmed
terrestrial breeder; eggs develop directly into froglets with no tadpole stage

voxel_model.pattern: sandy speckled back, huge bulging eyes

entries.notes: The internet's favourite frog; thrives without standing water in the Namib's fog belt. Vulnerable to strip-mining.

entries.name: Tarantula hawk
behaviour: paralyzes a tarantula with a single sting and drags it back to a burrow as a living nursery
Schmidt sting index 4 — second only to the bullet ant
aposematic orange-and-black; almost nothing dares to eat it

voxel_model.pattern: midnight blue-black body, rust-orange wings

entries.notes: A flying hypodermic that hunts spiders bigger than itself; the state insect of New Mexico.

entries.name: Red harvester ant
behaviour: clears a bare disc of gravel around the nest entrance, up to 10 m across
colonies tunnel 4+ m deep holding 10,000 workers
its sting is 3 of 4 on the Schmidt scale — and the only food of the Texas horned lizard
entries.notes: The crater-building ant whose sting fields whole horned-lizard populations. Colonies run visible trails from dawn.

entries.name: Sacred scarab
behaviour: rolls a perfect ball backward with hind legs, navigating by stars and moonlight
six rays on the head, four on the forelegs — the living sun-disc of ancient Egypt
fights over fresh dung before anyone else arrives

voxel_model.pattern: metallic blue-green sheen on dark elytra

entries.notes: The sun itself rolling across the Nile plain; the most religiously loaded beetle on Earth.

entries.name: Namib fog-basking beetle
behaviour: tilts its body head-down on dune crests in fog to harvest drinking water on its back
bundles of bumps on its elytra bead fog into droplets that run to its mouth
flightless and submerged in sand for up to 18 hours a day to dodge heat

voxel_model.pattern: fused matte black elytra, waxy sheen on bumps

entries.notes: The beetle that invented the water bottle; fog-harvest biomimetics is built on its back.
